about: Lot 310 (external bug hunt, edition 1.4: BUG-88, BUG-103; the mini-hunt's variants): an unlinked file (an O_TMPFILE in the user's home) executed through every spelling of its descriptor a caller can write — /proc/thread-self/fd/N, /proc/self/task/<tid>/fd/N, /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/fd/N, /dev/stdin, a relative fd/3 from a /proc/self working directory, a doubled slash, a `.` segment, a symlink in the home, /proc/<pid>/exe, map_files, /dev/fd/N — each R004's kill in LSM mode (the file's own flag decides); an unlinked file named systemd-executor under /opt/app or /usr/local, no identity of the packaged executor, killed; in tracepoint mode the per-thread names and /dev/stdin, killed. Controls: a memfd killed; systemd's launch of a unit (the linked executor through its descriptor) and an ordinary binary, nothing. On main the per-thread names, /dev/stdin, the relative path, the symlink, /proc/<pid>/exe and map_files ran the unlinked file without a verdict, and the files named systemd-executor were exempt.
